source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: The leading commercial products of the time (Notescan, Midiscan, PhotoScore, SmartScore, SharpEye) could not identify all musical symbols; they did quite well on typeset and printed music and poorly on handwritten music.
plan_bearing: Sets an honest expectation for the outcome: even mature products need correction.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: A typical OMR system has four stages: image preprocessing; recognition of musical symbols; reconstruction of the musical information into a logical description; construction of a notation model as a symbolic description of the sheet.
attributed_to: Rebelo et al. [83]; Bainbridge and Bell [3] for the generic framework
plan_bearing: Our pipeline maps onto it: straighten = stage 1; structure and voice events = stage 2; the page model and its checks = stage 3; the conversion = stage 4.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Preprocessing may apply enhancement, binarization, noise removal, blurring, and de-skewing; the staff line thickness and the distance between staff lines are computed and give the basic scale for all relative size comparisons.
plan_bearing: Supports Dann's design-software tools (despeckle, deskew) and principle 1, the staff as the ruler.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Symbol recognition is usually three parts: staff line detection and removal; segmentation of symbol primitives; recognition of the symbols.
plan_bearing: Matches the reader's existing stages.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: In reconstruction, graphical and syntactic rules bring in context to validate the recognition stage's results and resolve its ambiguities; symbols are then given musical meaning.
plan_bearing: Precedent for the sanity checks deciding, not only flagging (plan section 8, departure 3).

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Some systems use a voting scheme that merges the best features of several OMR algorithms to get better results.
attributed_to: Byrd and Schindele [13]; Knopke and Byrd [55]
plan_bearing: A precedent for voting, though across engines, not across the signs of one system as in principle 3.
notes: Read the primaries before citing them.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Most published work scanned at 300 dpi, some at 400 or 600; no study had evaluated how the methods depend on resolution.
plan_bearing: Matches what we measured: the staff count for one page changed with the raster. Supports resizing every page to one staff size.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: The most common preprocessing techniques for scores are enhancement, binarization, noise removal, blurring, de-skewing, and morphological operations.
plan_bearing: The design-software tool set Dann named at 22:22, as the field's standard list.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Binarization eases later steps but often introduces artifacts, so its advantage across the whole OMR process is not clear.
plan_bearing: The Jurgenson scan is already two-tone; for grey scans and photocopies, keep the grey original as the witness.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: A binarization method was proposed that uses the image's own content, the staff line thickness and spacing, to guide the threshold; it was the only content-aware method known to the authors.
plan_bearing: Clean relative to the staff, never by fixed amounts.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Most algorithms rely on an estimate of staff line thickness and staff spacing so that later processing is independent of predetermined magic numbers; fixed thresholds make a system hard to adapt to new situations.
plan_bearing: The audit's error 7: the reader is tuned to a corpus by fixed constants. The field's remedy is the one in principle 4: measure from the page.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Run-length coding of each image column gives the reference lengths: the most common black run is the line thickness and the most common white run is the spacing.
plan_bearing: Ilya already does this (`reader.py:250`, `staff_space_from_runs`).

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: On noisy scores with pale, broken lines the plain estimate fails (one example gives 1 and 1 against a true 5 and 19); a more robust estimate takes the most common sum of two consecutive vertical runs.
plan_bearing: Ilya's estimate is already the sum form: 'black-plus-following-white run' (`reader.py:251`). Relevant to degraded photocopies.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Removing staff lines simplifies later tasks at the risk of introducing noise: symbols are often broken, or leftover line fragments are read as symbols. Several authors work without removing the lines.
plan_bearing: Supports keeping the untouched image and using masks, as the reader's own ruling does (`reader.py:703-705`).

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Distorted staff lines are a common problem in printed as well as handwritten scores: lines are often not straight or horizontal, and sometimes hardly parallel to one another.
plan_bearing: Exactly what Tchaikovsky page 2 shows (drift growing from 5 px to 59 px down the page).

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: The simplest staff finder takes local maxima of the horizontal projection of black pixels, assuming straight horizontal lines; the page can be projected at several rotation angles and the best kept.
plan_bearing: This is the reader's current method and its known weakness (audit error 1). The desk's rotation test on page 2 is this method failing.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Other methods build staves from short staff segments, linking segments horizontally and vertically and merging overlaps; one treats a staff line segment as a horizontal chain of vertical black runs of uniform height, validated by its neighbours.
attributed_to: Miyao and Okamoto 2004 [63]; Szwoch 2005 [95]; Dutta et al. 2010 [32]; Dalitz et al. 2008 [26]
plan_bearing: Precedent for the strip trace in `proto-trace-staves_r1_2026-10-01.py`.
notes: Names checked against the survey's reference list. Read the primaries before citing.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: All the staff-detection methods have limits; lines with curvature or with breaks are inadequately resolved, and only a few works try to handle breaks.
plan_bearing: Broken staff and system lines on photocopies are a known open problem, not a solved one.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: A staff line can be found as the shortest connected path between the left and right margins that runs almost entirely through black pixels, a global optimization; it was tested on 32 synthetic scores with applied deformations and 40 real handwritten scores.
plan_bearing: A named alternative if the strip trace misses its gate: the 'stable paths' approach. Belongs in the plan's pivots.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: The main obstacles to isolating symbols come from printing, digitization, and paper degradation: distorted staff lines, broken and overlapping symbols, varying sizes and shapes, and dense zones.
plan_bearing: Dann's 'detangling' is the field's central difficulty.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: The usual approach is hierarchical: the sheet is split by staves, then elementary symbols are extracted (noteheads, rests, dots, stems, flags).
plan_bearing: The page model's hierarchy (page, system, staff, bar, event) is the standard shape.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: One system for printed scores produces several recognition hypotheses per symbol and makes the final decision with a fuzzy model, from consistency between symbols.
plan_bearing: Close to principle 6 (read, deduced, unsure) and principle 3 (signs vote). The survey calls this a good methodology for printed music (p. 187).
notes: Read the primary; it is the nearest published design to ours.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: One system detects barlines from their height and from the absence of noteheads at their ends.
plan_bearing: A barline test that complements the cross-staff vote.
notes: Name checked against the survey's reference list. That work is on old handwritten scores.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Classifiers with a reject option attach a confidence measure and decline to classify uncertain patterns such as broken or touching symbols, which are then handled manually; this minimizes misclassification.
plan_bearing: The field's name for 'unsure': reject and hand to the person.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Lyrics make a music document more complex. One work extracts lyric lines by computing baselines for lyrics and notes after staff removal, noting that lyric baselines can be highly curved; an overview of lyric recognition stresses associating lyrics with notes.
plan_bearing: Thin support for the lyric guide: the lyric line is a baseline, and it may curve. Tested on medieval sources, not on engraved song.
notes: The survey gives lyrics one paragraph. Names checked against the survey's reference list.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
section_heading: 5 Musical notation construction and final representation
claim: Music layout is two-dimensional, with pitch vertical and time horizontal, so position carries meaning: the same shape means different things in different places, and telling a tie from a slur needs the pitches of the two notes.
plan_bearing: Principle 1's grid, and the test for ties that the plan now includes.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
section_heading: 5 Musical notation construction and final representation
claim: Several systems formalize musical knowledge as a grammar that says how primitives combine into valid musical events; its proponent argues it reduces errors that come from using only very local information.
plan_bearing: Supports checks at the level of the bar and system. No statistical results were available for the grammar system cited.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
section_heading: 5 Musical notation construction and final representation
claim: One system applies graphical rules (an accidental sits before its notehead at the same height; a dot follows or sits above a notehead; other symbols cannot overlap) and then syntactic rules on tonality, accidentals, and metre, checking the number of beats per bar at the end.
plan_bearing: Bar arithmetic as a check, in a system for printed scores.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
section_heading: 5 Musical notation construction and final representation
claim: In another line of work the key and time signatures supply global information that is used to detect and correct recognition errors.
plan_bearing: Precedent for a check that corrects, not only flags.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
section_heading: 5 Musical notation construction and final representation
claim: One proposed architecture lets the interpretation stage feed back to the recognition stage; no practical results were known for it.
plan_bearing: Feedback is an old idea with little demonstrated practice by 2012. A caution against over-building it.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: OMR systems of the time did not adapt or improve through use, and most failed when the input was highly degraded, such as photocopies or low-quality paper.
plan_bearing: Degraded photocopies are where the field itself reports failure. The plan's hardening phase should be sized with that in mind.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Vendors claimed about 90 percent recognition accuracy; the authors call this unreliable because neither the scores used nor the method of estimation is stated.
plan_bearing: Vendor accuracy claims are not evidence. Our gates need a stated test set and a stated measure.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: What 'recognition' means depends on the goal, which blocks a common yardstick; proposals call for a standard dataset, a defined set of rules and metrics, and separate ratios for each kind of error.
attributed_to: Bellini et al. [6]; Jones et al. [51]
plan_bearing: Supports scoring in the facts a singer needs (bars, pitch, length, syllable under note), with a ratio per kind of error.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Comparing MusicXML files is one evaluation strategy, but the same score can be correctly written as different MusicXML, which makes one-to-one comparison difficult.
plan_bearing: The scorer must compare musical facts, not file text.

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: Global constraints can reduce missing, confused, and falsely detected symbols, for example by asking whether the detected durations in each bar add up to the time signature.
plan_bearing: Direct support for bar arithmetic as evidence (plan section 8, departure 3).

source_file: Rebelo_A et al (2012) - Optical Music Recognition State-of-the-Art and Open Issues - IJMIR 001_03 173-190.pdf
claim: A fully automatic, robust system for handwritten scores seems hard to achieve, so interactive OMR, with the user in the process, may be the realistic and practical solution; learning from expert users' corrections has been proposed.
plan_bearing: Said of handwritten music, but it is the same design as the singer's one tap, and it suggests keeping each correction as a labelled example.
